title: Cap. 7 Patrum: Remigius — Son delivered for predestined elect alone
pass_a_gloss: 5. Let Remigius, Bishop of Rheims, follow Ambrose, who writes thus on Romans 8: Those whom he predestined or predetermined to reign with him in eternal blessedness, these he called, these also he justified through his passion, through baptism and faith adorned with good works, and he justified them unto the end of the age. A little later, on these words, Who spared not his own Son — that is, says Remigius, he did not keep him from death, but for all of us predestined to eternal life he delivered him. All which things demonstrate that Christ suffered for the elect, and for the elect alone, with a sure purpose of saving them: which is the very special intention that we are trying to establish, and that we maintain must be restricted to the elect alone, in this offering of Christ.
pass_b_english: 5. After Ambrose comes Remigius of Rheims on Romans 8: Those he predestined — or marked out beforehand — to reign with him in eternal blessedness he also called and justified through his passion, through baptism and faith adorned with good works, and he justified them to the world's end. Soon after, on Who did not spare his own Son, Remigius says: he did not keep him from death, but delivered him for all of us predestined to eternal life. That shows Christ suffered for the elect, and for them alone, with a fixed purpose to save them — the very special intention we are establishing, and which we insist must be limited to the elect alone in this offering of Christ.
source_text: 5. Ambrosium sequatur Remigius Episcopus Rhemensis, qui haec scribit, in Rom. viii. Quos praedestinavit sive praefinivit secum regnaturos in aeterna beatitudine, hos vocavit, hos & justificavit per passionem suam, per baptismum & fidem exornatam bonis operibus, & justificavit usque ad finem seculi. Paulo post, in haec verba, Qui proprio Filio non pepercit, id est, inquit Remigius, a morte non servavit, sed pro nobis omnibus praedestinatis ad vitam aeternam illum tradidit. Quae omnia demonstrant Christum pro electis, & solis electis, cum proposito certo eosdem salvandi passum: quae est ipsissima specialis intentio, quam nos stabilire conamur, quamque ad solos electos restringendam tuemur, in hac Christi oblatione.
